questions.q: Each time a small CSV file lands in S3, a team must validate its header and row count. Each check takes about 3 minutes. They want the lowest cost and fastest start. Which service should run the check?

options.t: A Glue Spark ETL job on G.1X workers
options.why: Wrong: Spark start-up time and DPU billing are overkill for a 3-minute task.

options.t: A Glue Python shell job with 1 DPU
options.why: Wrong: it works, but Lambda is cheaper and starts faster for short event-driven work.

options.t: AWS Lambda triggered by the S3 upload
options.why: Right: small, fast, event-driven work under 15 minutes is Lambda's sweet spot.

options.t: An EMR cluster with a step per file
options.why: Wrong: a cluster to run and pay for, far too heavy for a tiny check.

questions.explain: Short event-driven tasks under 15 minutes go to Lambda, not Glue.
questions.remember: Glue = serverless Spark for GB-TB ETL. Tiny, fast, event-driven work under 15 minutes → Lambda.
variants: The task runs longer than 15 minutes with plain Python, no Spark → Glue Python shell job.
The task is a pure SQL reshape of S3 data → Athena CTAS/INSERT.
Full control of Spark or long-lived clusters → EMR.

questions.q: A team must run a one-time historical backfill with Glue 5.1. It is not urgent and can start late. They want the lowest DPU price. Which configuration fits?

options.t: Flex execution class with G.1X or G.2X workers
options.why: Right: Flex is about $0.29 per DPU-hour vs $0.44 standard, for non-urgent runs on G.1X/G.2X.

options.t: Flex execution class with G.16X workers
options.why: Wrong: G.12X, G.16X and R types do not support Flex.

options.t: Standard execution class with R.4X workers
options.why: Wrong: memory-optimized workers cost the standard rate and start slower; nothing here needs them.

options.t: Standard execution class with the maximum worker count
options.why: Wrong: more workers adds cost without lowering the price per DPU-hour.

questions.explain: Flex trades a slower, less certain start for a lower DPU-hour price.
questions.remember: Non-urgent Glue runs (tests, backfills, overnight batch) → Flex on Glue 3.0+ with G.1X or G.2X only.
variants: The run is time-sensitive and must start at once → Standard execution class.
Data size varies a lot per night → turn on Auto Scaling with a sensible maximum.
Big types (G.12X/G.16X/R) are needed → Flex is not available for them.

questions.q: A daily Glue job has job bookmarks set to Enable, yet every run reprocesses files it already handled. Which two script problems can cause this? (Choose 2.)

options.t: The job runs with the Flex execution class
options.why: Wrong: execution class does not affect bookmark state.

options.t: The script never calls `job.commit()`
options.why: Right: without commit the bookmark state is not saved for the next run.

options.t: The output is written as Parquet
options.why: Wrong: the output format does not affect source tracking.

options.t: Sources and transforms have no `transformation_ctx`
options.why: Right: bookmarks track only nodes that have a transformation_ctx.

questions.explain: Bookmarks need job.init(), job.commit() and a transformation_ctx on each tracked node.
questions.remember: Bookmark reprocessing → check job.commit(), transformation_ctx, max concurrency = 1, rewritten source files and non-sequential JDBC keys.
variants: Error 'version mismatch' → concurrent runs of a bookmarked job; keep max concurrency at 1.
An old S3 file was rewritten → S3 bookmarks use last-modified time, so it is read again.
Streaming or Python shell jobs → bookmarks do not apply (streaming uses checkpoints).

questions.q: After fixing a logic bug, a team must reprocess all S3 input once with a bookmarked Glue batch job, without creating duplicate output. What should they do?

options.t: Set the bookmark option to Pause for the next run
options.why: Wrong: Pause reads new data only and does not reread everything.

options.t: Delete the job's checkpoint folder in S3
options.why: Wrong: checkpoints are for streaming jobs, not batch bookmarks.

options.t: Raise maximum concurrency to 2 and rerun
options.why: Wrong: concurrent runs break bookmarks with a version mismatch.

options.t: Reset the bookmark with `reset-job-bookmark` and write to a clean or new target
options.why: Right: reset rereads all sources, and since targets are not cleaned you must avoid duplicates yourself.

questions.explain: Reset or rewind changes only source tracking; target files stay.
questions.remember: Reprocess with bookmarks → reset (or rewind) the bookmark, and handle the target yourself because Glue does not clean outputs.
variants: Backfill from a specific earlier run → rewind the bookmark to that run.
A streaming job must reprocess → delete its checkpoint folder.
Deleting the job also deletes its bookmark.

questions.q: A Glue job reads JSON files where the `amount` field is a number in some files and a string in others. A plain Spark DataFrame turns the column into strings. What is the Glue-native fix?

options.t: Use ApplyMapping to drop the field
options.why: Wrong: it loses the data instead of resolving the type.

options.t: Read as a DynamicFrame and resolve the choice type with `resolveChoice` (for example cast)
options.why: Right: DynamicFrames keep mixed types as a choice type you resolve on purpose.

options.t: Run the crawler again with a new classifier
options.why: Wrong: the files still contain mixed types; the job must resolve them.

options.t: Convert the input to Avro first
options.why: Wrong: changing format does not resolve conflicting types in the data.

questions.explain: Mixed types become a choice type in a DynamicFrame; resolveChoice settles it.
questions.remember: Messy or changing data → DynamicFrame, then resolveChoice (cast, make_cols, make_struct, project, match_catalog).
variants: Keep both types as separate columns → resolveChoice make_cols.
Cast to the types in the Catalog table → resolveChoice match_catalog.
Need Spark SQL or joins afterwards → toDF(), then DynamicFrame.fromDF() to come back.

questions.q: Nested JSON with arrays of line items must be loaded into tables in an RDS PostgreSQL database. Which Glue transform prepares it?

options.t: Relationalize
options.why: Right: it turns nested and array data into a set of flat tables linked by keys.

options.t: Unnest
options.why: Wrong: it flattens nested structs into columns but does not split arrays into related tables.

options.t: Spigot
options.why: Wrong: it only writes a sample to S3 for checking.

options.t: ApplyMapping
options.why: Wrong: it renames and casts fields; it does not split arrays into tables.

questions.explain: Relationalize = nested/array data to several flat relational tables.
questions.remember: Nested JSON to a relational database → Relationalize; flatten structs into columns only → Unnest.
variants: Only rename and retype columns → ApplyMapping (unlisted fields are dropped).
Merge staged updates by primary key → mergeDynamicFrame (staging records win).
Check a sample of output → Spigot.

questions.q: At month-end, many Glue job runs fail because the account hits its concurrent-run quota. The team wants runs to wait instead of failing. What should they enable?

options.t: Retries set to 10 on every job
options.why: Wrong: retries re-bill each attempt and do not wait for capacity in a controlled way.

options.t: Flex execution class
options.why: Wrong: Flex lowers price; it does not queue runs that exceed a quota.

options.t: Job run queuing
options.why: Right: runs that cannot start due to quota or temporary capacity wait in a queue.

options.t: A longer job timeout
options.why: Wrong: the run never started, so the timeout does not help.

questions.explain: Job run queuing makes runs wait (WAITING) instead of failing on quota limits.
questions.remember: Hitting the concurrent-run quota in peaks → job run queuing (and ask for a quota raise).
variants: A VPC job runs out of subnet IPs after launch (for executors) → it still fails; queuing does not help.
Run-level queuing setting overrides the job-level setting.
Throttling on API calls → retries with backoff or higher quotas.

questions.q: A Glue 5.1 job was created with a blank timeout. A large backfill run stops after 8 hours with status TIMEOUT and is not retried. What should the team do?

options.t: Set retries to 3 so the job restarts after the timeout
options.why: Wrong: jobs that time out are not retried.

options.t: Switch to Glue 4.0 to get a 48-hour default
options.why: Wrong: downgrading to change a default is the wrong fix; set the value you need.

options.t: Raise maximum concurrency
options.why: Wrong: concurrency allows parallel runs; it does not extend one run.

options.t: Set the job timeout explicitly to the expected runtime (up to 7 days)
options.why: Right: the 5.0+ default is 480 minutes; the max is 10,080 minutes.

questions.explain: Blank timeout = 480 min on 5.0+, 2,880 min on 4.0 and older; max 7 days.
questions.remember: Set a timeout that matches the expected runtime: defaults differ by version (8 h for 5.0+, 48 h for 4.0 and older), max 7 days, timeouts are not retried.
variants: A job might hang for days → set a tight timeout plus a delay notification threshold.
A streaming job with blank timeout → it restarts after 7 days (or in the maintenance window).
Retries: 0 to 10, and each retry is billed.

questions.q: Athena, Redshift Spectrum and EMR Spark must all query the same S3 data using one shared schema, with the least operational overhead. What should hold the metadata?

options.t: SageMaker Catalog
options.why: Wrong: it is the business catalog (glossary, discovery), not the technical metastore engines query.

options.t: The AWS Glue Data Catalog
options.why: Right: all three engines read it, and it is a drop-in Hive metastore replacement.

options.t: Glue Schema Registry
options.why: Wrong: it governs streaming message schemas, not tables at rest.

options.t: A self-managed Hive metastore on EC2
options.why: Wrong: works, but you must run and patch it.

questions.explain: The Glue Data Catalog is the shared technical metadata store for AWS analytics engines.
questions.remember: One schema shared by Athena, Spectrum, EMR, Glue and Lake Formation → Glue Data Catalog (one per account per Region).
variants: Business glossary and data discovery for analysts → SageMaker Catalog.
Stream schema contracts between producers and consumers → Glue Schema Registry.
EMR must use it → enable the Glue Catalog as the Hive metastore.

questions.q: A crawler runs on `s3://lake/events/`, which holds two different JSON schemas in subfolders. Afterwards, Athena returns zero rows from the tables. What is the fix?

options.t: Run `MSCK REPAIR TABLE` in Athena
options.why: Wrong: the issue is table grouping, not missing partitions.

options.t: Set the recrawl policy to crawl new folders only
options.why: Wrong: this limits what is scanned; it does not fix the grouping.

options.t: Add a custom JSON classifier
options.why: Wrong: format detection is fine; the tables map to the wrong prefixes.

options.t: Give each schema's root folder its own include path
options.why: Right: Athena maps one table to one prefix, so separate include paths give clean tables.

questions.explain: Mixed schemas under one prefix make the crawler build several tables, and Athena then sees nothing.
questions.remember: Athena zero rows after a crawl → crawler split one prefix into several tables; use one include path per table root.
variants: Files under one path are compatible → 'Create a single schema for each include path'.
Tell the crawler at which folder depth the table starts → table level setting.
Skip some files or folders → exclude patterns.

questions.q: A bucket holds millions of objects and new partitions arrive every hour. A crawler that rescans everything is slow and costly. Which crawler setting is best?

options.t: Recrawl policy 'Crawl based on events' using S3 event notifications through SQS
options.why: Right: it lists only changed subfolders, the fastest option for big prefixes.

options.t: Recrawl policy 'Crawl all folders' on an hourly schedule
options.why: Wrong: the default rereads everything each time, the costly behavior.

options.t: A larger crawler table threshold
options.why: Wrong: it caps how many tables are created; it does not speed scanning.

options.t: Two crawlers started by one trigger on the same path
options.why: Wrong: duplicate work, and it does not reduce listing.

questions.explain: Event-mode crawls use S3 events to visit only changed folders.
questions.remember: Big prefix with steady new data → event-mode crawler (or crawl new folders only); avoid full recrawls on unchanged data.
variants: Only new partitions, no event setup → 'Crawl new folders only' (does not change the existing schema).
Partitions are fully predictable (dates) and only Athena queries them → Athena partition projection.
The loading job knows the partition → ALTER TABLE ADD PARTITION or BatchCreatePartition.

questions.q: A Glue job writes partitioned Parquet output each night. The new partitions must appear in the Data Catalog in the same run, with no crawler. What should the job use?

options.t: A `push_down_predicate` on the sink
options.why: Wrong: pushdown predicates filter partitions on read, not on write.

options.t: Athena partition projection on the source table
options.why: Wrong: projection computes partitions for Athena only and stores none in the Catalog.

options.t: A Catalog sink with `enableUpdateCatalog=true`, `updateBehavior` and `partitionKeys`
options.why: Right: the job writes the data and updates the Catalog in one run.

options.t: Job bookmarks set to Enable
options.why: Wrong: bookmarks track input already read; they do not register output partitions.

questions.explain: enableUpdateCatalog lets an ETL job add partitions as it writes.
questions.remember: Job writes new partitions and the Catalog must follow in the same run → enableUpdateCatalog + updateBehavior + partitionKeys.
variants: Partitions still missing after the job → check enableUpdateCatalog is true and the schema matches or updateBehavior is UPDATE_IN_DATABASE.
Tables with Lake Formation cell-level filters → enableUpdateCatalog is not supported.
Hive-style folders already exist and you want a one-off fix → Athena MSCK REPAIR TABLE.

questions.q: A Glue job reads a Catalog table with 5 million date partitions. Planning takes much longer than the read, even with a `push_down_predicate`. What should the team do?

options.t: Increase the number of G.2X workers
options.why: Wrong: partition listing happens on the driver side; more workers do not fix it.

options.t: Add a partition index and use `catalogPartitionPredicate` in `additional_options`
options.why: Right: it prunes partitions on the server using the index instead of listing all of them.

options.t: Filter with `.filter()` after reading
options.why: Wrong: it reads everything first and saves nothing.

options.t: Run `MSCK REPAIR TABLE` before each job
options.why: Wrong: it adds partitions; it does not speed lookups.

questions.explain: push_down_predicate runs after listing all partitions; catalogPartitionPredicate uses indexes server-side.
questions.remember: Millions of partitions and slow planning → partition indexes + catalogPartitionPredicate (DynamicFrames) or partition projection for Athena.
variants: Athena must use the index → table property `partition_filtering.enabled = true`.
Redshift Spectrum, EMR and Glue Spark DataFrames use active indexes automatically.
Max 3 indexes per table, and the index's first key must appear in the filter.

questions.q: A Kafka producer on Amazon MSK keeps changing record fields and consumers crash. The team wants bad schema changes rejected before they reach consumers. What should they use?

options.t: A Glue crawler on the Kafka topic
options.why: Wrong: crawlers cannot crawl Kinesis or Kafka.

options.t: Glue Schema Registry with BACKWARD compatibility
options.why: Right: new versions are checked at registration, so incompatible changes are rejected.

options.t: Glue Schema Registry with compatibility NONE
options.why: Wrong: NONE does no checks; it is for development only.

options.t: Glue Data Quality rules on the Catalog table
options.why: Wrong: they check data at rest, not schema versions of messages in flight.

questions.explain: Schema Registry enforces stream schema contracts with compatibility modes.
questions.remember: Stop producers from breaking consumers on Kafka/Kinesis → Glue Schema Registry with BACKWARD (or FULL) compatibility. It is free.
variants: Consumers on the old schema must read new data → FORWARD.
Both directions → FULL; check against every earlier version → the _ALL variants.
Block all new versions → DISABLED.

questions.q: A schema in Glue Schema Registry uses BACKWARD compatibility. Adding a new Avro field `discount` is rejected. What is the likely cause?

options.t: BACKWARD mode does not allow any new fields
options.why: Wrong: BACKWARD allows adding optional fields and deleting fields.

options.t: The registry has reached 100 schemas
options.why: Wrong: the limits are 100 registries and 10,000 schema versions per Region; that would not give a compatibility error.

options.t: The new field is required: its type does not include `null`
options.why: Right: adding a required field breaks BACKWARD; make it optional.

options.t: Avro is not supported by Schema Registry
options.why: Wrong: Avro, JSON Schema and Protobuf are supported.

questions.explain: In Avro, optional = `null` in the type. Required additions break BACKWARD.
questions.remember: BACKWARD: new readers read old data → you may delete fields or add optional ones. Adding a required field breaks it.
variants: Removing a required field is rejected → that breaks FORWARD.
FULL mode → only add or remove optional fields.
A streaming job's table uses the schema → stop the job, update the table, restart.

questions.q: A team turns on Data Catalog metadata encryption with a KMS key. An audit shows older table definitions are still stored unencrypted. What explains this?

options.t: Metadata encryption applies only to metadata written after it is turned on
options.why: Right: existing metadata stays unencrypted until it is rewritten.

options.t: The KMS key is disabled
options.why: Wrong: a disabled key would make Catalog jobs and crawlers fail, not leave old data plain.

options.t: A Glue security configuration must also be attached to the Catalog
options.why: Wrong: security configurations cover job/crawler output, logs and bookmarks, not Catalog metadata.

options.t: Connection password encryption was not enabled
options.why: Wrong: that setting covers only passwords stored in connections.

questions.explain: Catalog encryption covers new metadata only.
questions.remember: Catalog metadata encryption (KMS) is forward-only; old metadata stays plain until rewritten. Connection password encryption is a separate setting.
variants: Jobs and crawlers fail after the key was disabled or deleted → re-enable the key.
Encrypt job output, logs and bookmarks → a Glue security configuration.
Partition indexes cannot be created on encrypted partitions.

questions.q: Athena queries on raw CSV and JSON logs in S3 are slow and costly. Most queries filter by event date. What should a Glue job produce?

options.t: Gzip-compressed CSV files
options.why: Wrong: smaller, but gzip text cannot be split and Athena still scans every column.

options.t: Parquet files partitioned by `user_id`
options.why: Wrong: high-cardinality partitions create huge metadata and small files.

options.t: Snappy Parquet files partitioned by date
options.why: Right: columnar reads plus partition pruning cut the data scanned.

options.t: Avro files with no partitions
options.why: Wrong: row-based and no pruning; Avro fits streaming and schema evolution.

questions.explain: Columnar format plus a moderate-cardinality partition on the filter column.
questions.remember: Slow, costly text-format queries → convert to Parquet (snappy) partitioned by the filter column, usually date. Never partition on a high-cardinality column.
variants: Data is streamed with evolving schemas → Avro with Schema Registry.
Hive/EMR-centric stack → ORC is a similar columnar choice.
Aim for roughly 128 MB to 1 GB files to avoid the small-files problem.

questions.q: A Glue job reads 2 million small CSV files from one S3 prefix and spends most of its time on task overhead. What is the simplest fix in the read?

options.t: Set `groupFiles` to `inPartition` with a `groupSize`
options.why: Right: grouping packs small files into larger tasks and cuts overhead.

options.t: Call `repartition(1)` after the read
options.why: Wrong: the read overhead remains, and one partition kills parallelism.

options.t: Switch the job to a Python shell job
options.why: Wrong: no Spark, and it is far too small for millions of files.

options.t: Use the `s3a://` URI scheme
options.why: Wrong: s3a can fail with 'Failed to parse XML document' when listing many files; use s3://.

questions.explain: groupFiles/groupSize reduce tasks for many small text files.
questions.remember: Many small CSV/JSON files → groupFiles inPartition + groupSize, or compact them. Grouping is not supported for Parquet, ORC or Avro.
variants: More than 50,000 input files → Glue turns grouping on automatically.
The small files are Parquet → compaction (for example Iceberg optimization), not groupFiles.
The driver runs out of memory listing files → group files, partition well, tune bookmarks.

questions.q: A team builds a Glue streaming job that reads from an Amazon MSK topic and writes Parquet to S3. Which two setup steps are required? (Choose 2.)

options.t: Create a Glue Kafka connection using TLS bootstrap servers
options.why: Right: Kafka needs a connection, and plaintext is not supported.

options.t: Run a crawler on the topic to create the table
options.why: Wrong: crawlers cannot create Kinesis or Kafka tables.

options.t: Enable job bookmarks to track offsets
options.why: Wrong: streaming jobs use checkpoints, not bookmarks.

options.t: Create the stream's Data Catalog table manually in the Glue console or API
options.why: Right: stream tables are created by hand, and not through the Lake Formation console.

questions.explain: Kafka streams need a TLS connection and a hand-made Catalog table.
questions.remember: Glue streaming from Kafka/MSK → TLS Kafka connection (IAM auth on MSK is fine) + manually created Catalog table + Spark streaming job with checkpoints.
variants: The source is Kinesis → no connection needed.
Kinesis in another account → stream ARN plus an assumed role ARN.
Job has a VPC connection and reads Kinesis → add a Kinesis interface VPC endpoint.

questions.q: A fraud team needs sub-second, stateful, windowed analytics on a Kinesis stream. Which service fits best?

options.t: A Glue streaming job with a 100-second window
options.why: Wrong: Glue streaming is micro-batch; it is not built for sub-second stateful processing.

options.t: Glue DataBrew
options.why: Wrong: DataBrew is not for streaming.

options.t: A Glue batch job with bookmarks every 5 minutes
options.why: Wrong: batch cannot meet sub-second latency.

options.t: Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink
options.why: Right: it is designed for low-latency stateful windowed stream processing.

questions.explain: Glue streaming = micro-batch ETL; Flink = sub-second stateful analytics.
questions.remember: Continuous ETL from Kinesis/MSK into S3 with no servers → Glue streaming. Sub-second, stateful, windowed analytics → Managed Flink.
variants: Fresher Glue streaming output → smaller window (more small files).
A stream that only needs a few minutes of work a day → batch with bookmarks or Firehose to S3.
Plain delivery to S3 with little transformation → Firehose.

questions.q: DMS writes full-load and CDC files to S3. The lake tables must apply inserts, updates and deletes and support time travel. What should the Glue job write to?

options.t: Apache Iceberg tables registered in the Glue Data Catalog
options.why: Right: Iceberg adds ACID row-level changes, snapshots for time travel and schema evolution.

options.t: Plain Parquet files with job bookmarks
options.why: Wrong: bookmarks only skip old input; plain Parquet has no row-level updates.

options.t: CSV files partitioned by load date
options.why: Wrong: no transactions, no updates and no time travel.

options.t: A Glue Schema Registry schema
options.why: Wrong: the registry holds stream schemas, not table data.

questions.explain: Upserts, deletes and time travel on S3 need an open table format such as Iceberg.
questions.remember: CDC into the lake with upserts/deletes/time travel → Iceberg on the Glue Catalog (enable with --datalake-formats). Plain Parquet cannot update rows.
variants: Supported source and little transformation → zero-ETL instead of a pipeline.
Small files pile up in Iceberg → managed compaction in the Catalog.
Iceberg v2 → v3 upgrade is one-way; keep v2 if another reader cannot read v3.

questions.q: A Glue job that loads a large dataset into Amazon Redshift fails after about one hour with an 'S3 service token expired' error. What is the cause?

options.t: The job timeout is set to 60 minutes
options.why: Wrong: that would end with TIMEOUT, not a token error.

options.t: Redshift rejected the COPY because of a type mismatch
options.why: Wrong: that gives a load error, not an expired token.

options.t: The temporary credentials used for the S3 temp path expire after 1 hour
options.why: Right: Glue moves Redshift data through S3 with UNLOAD/COPY, and those credentials last 1 hour.

options.t: The job role lacks `iam:PassRole`
options.why: Wrong: the job would fail at creation or start, not after an hour.

questions.explain: Glue-Redshift traffic goes through --TempDir in S3 with 1-hour temporary credentials.
questions.remember: Glue reads/writes Redshift via an S3 temp path (UNLOAD/COPY). Long jobs can hit 1-hour token expiry → split the work.
variants: The job role or Redshift cannot reach the temp path → grant both access to it.
Glue created a temp bucket → check S3 Block Public Access.
Bulk loads without Glue → Redshift COPY from S3.

questions.q: In the Spark UI, one task in a join stage runs ten times longer than the others, and `glue.driver.skewness.stage` is above 0. Which change helps most?

options.t: Add more G.1X workers
options.why: Wrong: the stage still waits for the one slow task.

options.t: Switch to the Flex execution class
options.why: Wrong: Flex changes price and start time, not task balance.

options.t: Enable continuous CloudWatch logging
options.why: Wrong: helps watch the job, but does not fix the slow task.

options.t: Salt the hot key or enable Spark AQE skew-join settings
options.why: Right: spreading the hot key evens out task sizes.

questions.explain: Data skew = one key much bigger than others; fix the key distribution.
questions.remember: One long task, skewness metric > 0 (max task > 5× median) → salt keys, filter hot keys, AQE skew join, repartition. More workers do not help.
variants: Many workers idle all job long → too few partitions or over-provisioning; use Auto Scaling.
Joining a big table to a small one → broadcast the small side.
Python UDFs are slow → use built-in Spark functions.

questions.q: A Glue Spark job fails with 'Container killed by YARN for exceeding memory limits' on executors. Which two changes address this? (Choose 2.)

options.t: Set retries to 10
options.why: Wrong: each retry hits the same limit and is billed.

options.t: Use memory-optimized R workers or a bigger G worker
options.why: Right: more memory per executor holds the task's data.

options.t: Increase the number of partitions so each task is smaller
options.why: Right: smaller tasks need less memory each.

options.t: Switch to the Flex execution class
options.why: Wrong: Flex uses G.1X/G.2X and does not add memory.

options.t: Coalesce everything into one partition
options.why: Wrong: one huge task makes memory pressure worse.

questions.explain: Executor OOM → more memory per task or smaller tasks (and fix skew).
questions.remember: Executor OOM → bigger/R workers, more partitions, fix skew. Driver OOM → too many files listed or collect()/toPandas() on big data.
variants: 'No space left on device' → shuffle spill; bigger worker or less shuffle.
Driver OOM while listing S3 → group files, fewer files per partition.
Estimate executors needed → numberMaxNeededExecutors in CloudWatch.

questions.q: A company wants a fresh copy of Salesforce data in its SageMaker lakehouse on S3, with little transformation and no pipeline code. What should it use?

options.t: A Glue streaming job reading Salesforce
options.why: Wrong: Salesforce is not a streaming source for Glue streaming.

options.t: A Glue zero-ETL integration with Salesforce as the source
options.why: Right: managed replication into the lakehouse with no pipeline code.

options.t: Glue DataBrew recipe jobs
options.why: Wrong: DataBrew is for cleaning data, not managed replication.

options.t: A Glue crawler on the Salesforce API
options.why: Wrong: crawlers catalog data; they do not copy it.

questions.explain: Zero-ETL = managed replication when you only need a fresh copy.
questions.remember: Fresh copy of SaaS (Salesforce, SAP, ServiceNow...) or DynamoDB data, little transformation → Glue zero-ETL. Need to clean, join or mask → a Glue job.
variants: Source is a self-managed MySQL/PostgreSQL/Oracle/SQL Server → zero-ETL target must be Amazon Redshift.
Aurora to Redshift → Aurora's own zero-ETL integration.
Zero-ETL billing → no integration fee; pay ingestion volume plus target compute.

questions.q: A pipeline runs a Glue job, then an Athena query, then a Lambda function, then waits for a manager's approval, with retries and error branches. Which orchestrator fits?

options.t: A Glue workflow with conditional triggers
options.why: Wrong: Glue workflows chain only Glue jobs and crawlers.

options.t: A Glue scheduled trigger
options.why: Wrong: it only starts Glue jobs and crawlers on a time.

options.t: AWS Step Functions
options.why: Right: it calls Glue (startJobRun.sync), Athena and Lambda, with retry/catch, choice and human approval.

options.t: EventBridge Scheduler alone
options.why: Wrong: it starts things on a schedule but does not manage steps, branches or approvals.

questions.explain: Multi-service pipelines with error handling → Step Functions.
questions.remember: Only Glue jobs and crawlers → Glue workflow. Many services, retries, branching, approval → Step Functions. Existing Airflow DAGs → MWAA.
variants: The team already runs Airflow → MWAA (monthly cost even when idle).
React to an event such as a file landing → EventBridge starts the workflow or state machine.
Crawler → job → crawler inside Glue only → Glue workflow.

questions.q: Thousands of small files land in S3 each hour. A Glue workflow must start once per 100 files, or after at most 15 minutes if fewer arrive. How should it start?

options.t: A scheduled trigger every 15 minutes
options.why: Wrong: runs even when no files arrived and ignores the 100-file count.

options.t: An EventBridge event start trigger with batch size 100 and batch window 900 seconds
options.why: Right: whichever condition is met first starts the run; 900 s is the maximum window.

options.t: An EventBridge event start trigger with batch size 100 and batch window 3,600 seconds
options.why: Wrong: the maximum batch window is 900 seconds.

options.t: S3 Event Notifications to a conditional trigger
options.why: Wrong: conditional triggers watch job and crawler states, not S3 events.

questions.explain: Workflow EventBridge triggers batch events by size or window, whichever comes first.
questions.remember: Start a Glue workflow from S3 events → EventBridge event start trigger. Batch size default 1, window max 900 s, starting when the first event arrives.
variants: A run fails → that event batch is not reused; alert on failure so it is not lost.
Runs over the max concurrent workflow runs → not started and not retried.
One run per file → leave batch size at 1.

questions.q: A conditional trigger should start job B when job A succeeds. An engineer starts job A by hand from the console; it succeeds, but job B never starts. Why?

options.t: Dependent jobs fire only when the watched job was started by a trigger
options.why: Right: the chain must descend from a scheduled or on-demand trigger.

options.t: Conditional triggers can watch crawlers only
options.why: Wrong: they watch both jobs and crawlers.

options.t: The trigger must use ANY instead of ALL
options.why: Wrong: with one watched job, ANY and ALL behave the same.

options.t: SUCCEEDED is not a state a trigger can watch
options.why: Wrong: jobs can be watched for SUCCEEDED, STOPPED, FAILED and TIMEOUT.

questions.explain: A manual run does not fire conditional triggers.
questions.remember: Conditional triggers fire only for jobs started by a trigger; start the chain with a scheduled or on-demand trigger.
variants: Run a cleanup when either of two jobs fails → conditional trigger with ANY and FAILED.
Run job C after both A and B succeed → ALL with SUCCEEDED.
Pause a schedule without deleting it → deactivate the trigger.

questions.q: A Glue ETL job must load good rows into the curated zone and send rows that break completeness and range rules to a quarantine prefix. What should the team use?

options.t: Data Quality rules run on the Catalog table after the load
options.why: Wrong: the Catalog entry point cannot identify failed rows, and the data has already landed.

options.t: A DataBrew profile job
options.why: Wrong: it computes statistics; it does not split rows inside the ETL job.

options.t: Amazon Macie
options.why: Wrong: Macie finds sensitive data in S3, not rule failures.

options.t: The Evaluate Data Quality transform in the job with row-level outcomes
options.why: Right: in-job DQ marks each row's result so bad rows can be routed away.

questions.explain: Row-level failed-record identification exists only for DQ inside ETL jobs.
questions.remember: Quarantine bad rows / stop bad data before it lands → Evaluate Data Quality in the ETL job (row-level outcomes, no extra charge). Check data at rest with rule recommendations → Catalog DQ.
variants: Need suggested rules from a profile of the table → Catalog DQ rule recommendations.
Thresholds should follow history → dynamic rules or ML anomaly detection.
Nested or array columns fail DQ → flatten them first.

questions.q: Business analysts who do not write code must clean CSV files, view value distributions and outliers, and save cleaned Parquet to S3 on a daily schedule. Which service fits?

options.t: Glue Studio visual ETL with a Spark job
options.why: Wrong: no-code too, but aimed at engineers building production ETL, not analyst profiling and cleaning.

options.t: Glue streaming ETL
options.why: Wrong: there is no stream here.

options.t: AWS Glue DataBrew with profile jobs and a scheduled recipe job
options.why: Right: no-code preparation, profiling charts and scheduled jobs that write to S3.

options.t: Glue Schema Registry
options.why: Wrong: it manages stream schemas, not data cleaning.

questions.explain: DataBrew = no-code data preparation and profiling for analysts.
questions.remember: Analysts + no code + clean/profile data → DataBrew. Engineers building production ETL (joins, streaming, open table formats) → Glue Studio / Spark jobs.
variants: Run it every day → schedule the DataBrew job (or use Step Functions).
Very custom logic or streaming → Glue ETL, not DataBrew.
Rules for completeness/uniqueness in a pipeline → Glue Data Quality.

questions.q: A company must find unknown PII across many S3 buckets, and also mask PII columns while a Glue Spark job writes data to a shared analytics zone. Which two services or features meet these needs? (Choose 2.)

options.t: Amazon Macie to scan the S3 buckets
options.why: Right: Macie discovers PII stored in S3.

options.t: Glue Data Quality IsComplete rules
options.why: Wrong: they test completeness, not PII.

options.t: Glue Schema Registry
options.why: Wrong: it governs stream schemas, not sensitive data.

options.t: The Glue Detect Sensitive Data transform in the job
options.why: Right: it detects and masks PII during processing.

questions.explain: Macie finds PII at rest in S3; Glue's transform masks it in flight.
questions.remember: Discover PII in S3 → Macie. Mask PII inside a Glue job → Detect Sensitive Data. Hide columns from users → Lake Formation column/cell permissions.
variants: Analysts must de-identify data without code → DataBrew masking steps.
Users must not see a sensitive column at query time → Lake Formation column-level permissions.
Common chain: Macie finds → tag in Lake Formation → Glue masks.

questions.q: A developer creating a Glue job gets 'the role passed should be given assume role permissions for the Glue service'. What fixes it?

options.t: Attach `AWSGlueServiceRole` to the developer's user
options.why: Wrong: that managed policy belongs on the job role, and it does not grant PassRole.

options.t: Grant the developer `iam:PassRole` on the job role, and ensure the role trusts `glue.amazonaws.com`
options.why: Right: the creator must pass the role, and Glue must be able to assume it.

options.t: Add a resource policy on the Data Catalog
options.why: Wrong: that controls cross-account Catalog access, not role passing.

options.t: Add an S3 gateway endpoint
options.why: Wrong: a network fix for a permissions error.

questions.explain: PassRole for the creator, trust policy for glue.amazonaws.com on the role.
questions.remember: Glue role errors → creator needs iam:PassRole; the job role's trust must allow glue.amazonaws.com. AWSGlueServiceRole is a base; add your own S3/KMS/Secrets permissions.
variants: S3 Access Denied in a job → role S3 permission, bucket policy, or Lake Formation grants.
ec2:Describe* unauthorized errors in a VPC job → add those EC2 read actions to the job role.
Least privilege → scope the role to the needed S3 prefixes and Catalog databases.

questions.q: A Glue job with a VPC connection must read a private RDS database and S3 in the same Region. It fails at start-up. Which two network settings are required? (Choose 2.)

options.t: An internet gateway route on the job's subnet
options.why: Wrong: Glue workers use private ENIs; S3 is reached via an endpoint or NAT.

options.t: A security group with a self-referencing rule allowing all inbound TCP from itself
options.why: Right: Glue workers must talk to each other.

options.t: An S3 gateway VPC endpoint (or NAT gateway) for the subnet
options.why: Right: without it you get 'Could not find S3 endpoint or NAT gateway for subnetId'.

options.t: A public IP on the RDS instance
options.why: Wrong: the connection exists exactly so the job can reach private resources.

questions.explain: VPC Glue jobs need a self-referencing SG and a route to S3.
questions.remember: Glue in a VPC → self-referencing SG (all TCP inbound from itself, outbound all), S3 endpoint or NAT, DNS hostnames on, enough subnet IPs, and the DB SG allowing the Glue SG.
variants: 'No private DNS for network interface found' → turn on enableDnsHostnames.
'Resource unavailable' at start → out of ENIs or subnet IPs.
'Could not find subnet for AZ' → use a subnet in another AZ.

questions.q: A Glue job in a private subnet has a security configuration that encrypts output with SSE-KMS. It now fails with a 'kms timeout' error. What should be added?

options.t: A KMS interface VPC endpoint (or a NAT gateway)
options.why: Right: the job must reach KMS from the subnet.

options.t: An S3 gateway endpoint
options.why: Wrong: that gives an S3 route, not a KMS route.

options.t: Catalog metadata encryption
options.why: Wrong: unrelated to reaching KMS from the job.

options.t: A longer job timeout
options.why: Wrong: the call cannot reach KMS however long it waits.

questions.explain: Security configurations need network access to KMS from the VPC.
questions.remember: VPC job/crawler + security configuration → needs a KMS endpoint or NAT. Symptoms: 'kms timeout' (job), 'internal service exception' (crawler).
variants: Glue API privately from the VPC → Glue interface endpoint.
Secrets Manager or CloudWatch Logs unreachable → interface endpoints or NAT for those too.
The job role also needs kms:Encrypt, kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey on an ENABLED key.

questions.q: Compliance requires that a Glue job's S3 output, CloudWatch logs and job bookmarks are all encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What is the right setup?

options.t: Set the job parameter for SSE-S3 encryption
options.why: Wrong: SSE-S3 is not a customer key, and it covers S3 output only.

options.t: Turn on Data Catalog metadata encryption
options.why: Wrong: it encrypts Catalog metadata, not job output, logs or bookmarks.

options.t: Rely on S3 bucket default encryption
options.why: Wrong: it covers S3 objects only, not logs or bookmarks.

options.t: A Glue security configuration with SSE-KMS for S3, KMS for CloudWatch Logs and CSE-KMS for bookmarks
options.why: Right: one security configuration covers all three; the key policy must allow CloudWatch Logs.

questions.explain: A security configuration encrypts what Glue writes: S3 data, logs and bookmarks.
questions.remember: Encrypt job output, logs and bookmarks → Glue security configuration (overrides the SSE-S3 job parameter). Encrypt metadata → Catalog encryption.
variants: Log encryption fails → the KMS key policy must allow logs.<region>.amazonaws.com and the job roles.
Iceberg tables → set their own S3 SSE as well.
Encrypt connection passwords → Catalog connection password encryption.

questions.q: A Glue job in a private subnet with an S3 gateway endpoint reads one bucket fine but gets 'connect timed out' on a bucket in another Region. What is the fix?

options.t: Add a second S3 gateway endpoint for the other Region
options.why: Wrong: a gateway endpoint is Regional and only reaches buckets in its own Region.

options.t: Add a self-referencing security group rule
options.why: Wrong: workers talk fine; the problem is the route to the remote bucket.

options.t: Route the subnet through a NAT gateway for cross-Region S3 access
options.why: Right: a gateway S3 endpoint only reaches same-Region buckets.

options.t: Enable job run queuing
options.why: Wrong: the job started; this is a network route problem.

questions.explain: S3 gateway endpoints are same-Region only.
questions.remember: Cross-Region S3 from a private Glue subnet → NAT gateway (watch NAT data charges); same-Region → S3 gateway endpoint.
variants: 'Could not find S3 endpoint or NAT gateway' → add an S3 endpoint or NAT.
S3 Access Denied → IAM, bucket policy or Lake Formation, not routing.
Unexpected Glue bill → NAT data processing can be a hidden cost.

questions.q: CloudWatch shows `glue.driver.workerUtilization` around 20% for most runs of several Glue 5.1 jobs. Data volume varies each night. How should the team cut cost?

options.t: Turn on Auto Scaling with a sensible maximum number of workers
options.why: Right: workers are added and removed as stages need them, so idle capacity is not billed.

options.t: Move to G.4X workers
options.why: Wrong: bigger workers add idle capacity.

options.t: Increase retries
options.why: Wrong: retries add cost and do not help utilization.

options.t: Enable continuous logging
options.why: Wrong: useful for watching runs; does not change capacity.

questions.explain: Low worker utilization means over-provisioning; Auto Scaling matches demand.
questions.remember: Low workerUtilization or variable data → Auto Scaling (Glue 3.0+) with a sensible max; also right-size, use Flex for non-urgent runs and process less data.
variants: Non-urgent test or backfill → Flex.
Small stream → G.025X plus Auto Scaling.
Check real usage after a run → DPUSeconds in get-job-run.

questions.q: A Glue job reads a Lake Formation table that has cell-level data filters. The team notices job bookmarks and pushdown predicates stopped working. What is going on?

options.t: The job role is missing `s3:GetObject`
options.why: Wrong: missing S3 access would fail the read, not just these features.

options.t: The job must be upgraded to Glue 6.0
options.why: Wrong: the notes list these as limits of cell-filtered tables, not of a version.

options.t: It is expected: tables with cell-level filters do not support bookmarks, bounded execution or pushdown/catalog partition predicates
options.why: Right: these features are disabled for such tables.

options.t: The table needs a partition index
options.why: Wrong: catalog partition predicates are also unsupported on these tables.

questions.explain: Lake Formation cell-level filters switch off several Glue read features.
questions.remember: Lake Formation cell filters → no bookmarks, bounded execution, pushdown or catalog partition predicates, or enableUpdateCatalog. Job roles also need Lake Formation grants, not only S3.
variants: Another account must read tables with column limits → Lake Formation cross-account grants.
Grant by tag instead of table by table → LF tag-based access control.
Glue 5.0+ has built-in fine-grained access control integration.

questions.q: An analytics account must run Glue jobs on Data Catalog tables owned by a central account, seeing only some columns. Governance must be central. What is the preferred approach?

options.t: Copy the tables to the analytics account each night
options.why: Wrong: duplicate data and metadata with no central control.

options.t: Make the S3 bucket public with a prefix filter
options.why: Wrong: insecure and has no column control.

options.t: Use IAM users in the central account shared with the analytics team
options.why: Wrong: shared long-term credentials break least privilege.

options.t: Lake Formation cross-account grants with column-level permissions
options.why: Right: Lake Formation grants database/table/column/row access across accounts with central governance.

questions.explain: Fine-grained cross-account Catalog access → Lake Formation.
questions.remember: Cross-account Catalog access → Lake Formation grants (preferred, fine-grained) or Catalog resource policy + RAM. Job roles need the Lake Formation permissions.
variants: Only table-level sharing without fine-grained control → Catalog resource policy + AWS RAM.
Many tables classified by sensitivity → LF tag-based access control.
Audit who accessed data → Lake Formation and CloudTrail logs.

questions.q: A Glue JDBC connection to an RDS database stores the password in plain text, and a job parameter also contains it. What should the team do?

options.t: Move the password into a job parameter only
options.why: Wrong: job parameters are visible to anyone who can describe the job.

options.t: Encrypt the script in S3 and keep the password in it
options.why: Wrong: never hard-code secrets in scripts.

options.t: Turn on Catalog metadata encryption only
options.why: Wrong: it encrypts new metadata, but the password still sits in the job parameter and the connection.

options.t: Store it in Secrets Manager, reference the secret in the connection, and grant the job role `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`
options.why: Right: secrets stay out of code and parameters, and only the role can read them.

questions.explain: Glue credentials belong in Secrets Manager, referenced by the connection.
questions.remember: DB credentials for Glue → Secrets Manager referenced in the connection; job role needs secretsmanager:GetSecretValue. Never put secrets in scripts or job parameters.
variants: Passwords must stay in connections → enable Catalog connection password encryption (KMS).
Data in transit to the DB → enable SSL on the JDBC connection.
Kafka connection → TLS bootstrap servers only.
